title: Binary derived open descent for modules on a ringed topos
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a Grothendieck topos (a category of sheaves of sets on a small site), $R$ a commutative ring object of $\mathcal T$, and $D(\mathcal T,R)$ the ordinary derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ be subterminal objects (monomorphisms into the terminal object) whose union is $1$, and put $W=U\times V$. Write $\mathcal T/U$, $\mathcal T/V$, $\mathcal T/W$ for the slice topoi, $R_U,R_V,R_W$ for the restricted rings, and $j_Z^*$ for restriction to a slice. The exact extension-by-zero left adjoint is denoted $j_{Z!}$ and the derived right adjoint of restriction is denoted $Rj_{Z*}$, for $Z=U,V,W$.

(1) Given $A\in D(\mathcal T/U,R_U)$, $B\in D(\mathcal T/V,R_V)$ and an isomorphism $c:A|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}B|_W$, there exist $G\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ and isomorphisms $a:G|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A$, $b:G|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $b|_W=c\circ a|_W$. One may take $G$ in a distinguished triangle
$$G\longrightarrow Rj_{U*}A\oplus Rj_{V*}B\xrightarrow{(Rj_*c,-1)}Rj_{W*}(B|_W)\longrightarrow G[1],$$
where each component is the derived restriction-adjunction map, with $c$ applied in the first component. If $A,B$ have cohomology in a common interval $[a_0,b_0]$, so does $G$.

(2) For every $M\in D(\mathcal T,R)$ there is the natural distinguished open-cover triangle
$$j_{W!}(M|_W)\xrightarrow{(1,-1)}j_{U!}(M|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(M|_V)\xrightarrow{(1,1)}M\longrightarrow j_{W!}(M|_W)[1].$$
The arrows are the canonical nested-open maps and the adjunction counits. Restriction and extension by zero here act termwise on complexes. No uniqueness of a gluing of arbitrary derived morphisms is asserted.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), first assertion and its Rj_* cone construction; Tag 08BU (lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek). The ringed-space arguments are to be extended to open subtopoi of a ringed Grothendieck topos; this extension is the agent-stated prerequisite, not a claim that these tags already state it.

proof.text: Choose a small site $\mathcal S$ presenting $\mathcal T$. Starting with its sheafified representables and $1,U,V$, close a set of chosen objects under finite limits, by adjoining the limits of all finite diagrams at each of countably many stages. Such limits exist by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]; each stage is a set since the sheaf category has set-valued Hom sets. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-subcategory-comparison] to the resulting full subcategory $\mathcal E$, retaining the epimorphic families $\{C\times U,C\times V\}\to C$. They are epimorphic because $U\cup V=1$, and local surjectivity is preserved by pullback. This gives a small subcanonical site with $1,U,V,W$ represented by its objects. Under the nerve equivalence, a ring or module is sent to its sheaf of generalized sections $C\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(C,-)$; its operations are the induced operations on these sections. The inverse equivalence recovers the operations, since an equivalence preserves finite products and their diagrams of identities. Thus the ring and module categories are identified, including the slice categories as follows. A sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal E/Z$ corresponds to the sheaf $H(C)=\coprod_{s:C\to Z}F(C,s)$ over $h_Z$, with projection $(s,x)\mapsto s$. This is a sheaf: a matching family first glues its $s$ coordinates in $h_Z$, then glues its $x$ coordinates in $F$ on the localized site. Conversely take the fibre over $s$ of a sheaf $H\to h_Z$; the two constructions are inverse sectionwise. Ring and module operations are the same operations in each fibre, identifying modules over the restricted ring in both descriptions. These are additive exact equivalences: their inverse functors preserve kernels and cokernels by their universal properties. They induce derived equivalences by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], so it suffices to work on $\mathcal E$ and its localized sites.

source.place: Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence), including prescribed epimorphic covers; finite-limit closure and module/slice identifications written here

proof.text: On $\mathcal E/Z$, restriction and relocalization are the sectionwise functors of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], $j_Z^*$ and $j_{Z!}$ are exact, with $j_{Z!}\dashv j_Z^*$. The explicit presheaf in [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] is $P_F(C)=F(C\to Z)$ if $C\to Z$ exists, and $0$ otherwise, because $Z$ is subterminal; $j_{Z!}F=P_F^\#$. Restriction commutes with underlying abelian sheafification by [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification]; the comparison is module-linear since both actions are the extensions of the same sectionwise scalar action through the sheafification unit [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. For $C\to U$, a map $C\to V$ is exactly a map $C\to W$. The presheaf formula therefore gives $j_U^*j_{V!}F=k_{U!}(F|_W)$, where $k_U:W\to U$; taking $V=U$ gives $j_U^*j_{U!}F=F$. Interchanging the displayed names gives $j_V^*j_{U!}F=k_{V!}(F|_W)$ and $j_V^*j_{V!}F=F$. These comparisons preserve units, counits and nested-open maps, since before sheafification each nonzero component is the identity on the indicated summand.

For module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction to $U,V$ jointly detects zero objects: if $F|_U=F|_V=0$, a section of $F(C)$ restricts to zero on the covering $C\times U,C\times V$ from Step 1, hence is zero by the separatedness part of the sheaf condition. Exact restriction then detects exactness of any module sequence by applying this zero test to its kernel, cokernel and middle homology. Also, exact restriction commutes with $H^q=\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently it detects vanishing of cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms of complexes.

source.place: Section 03CV, sheaf condition and sectionwise kernels; exactness tested on the binary subterminal cover

proof.text: The module categories on $\mathcal E$ and all its slices have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For a K-injective $I$ and an acyclic complex $L$ on a slice, the termwise adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(L,j_Z^*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(j_{Z!}L,I)=0$, since $j_{Z!}$ is exact. Thus restriction preserves K-injectives, directly from [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For a K-injective $J$ on the slice, $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(L,j_{Z*}J)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(j_Z^*L,J)=0$ for every acyclic $L$ on the ambient site, so direct image preserves K-injectives as well. Here $j_Z^*\dashv j_{Z*}$ is the module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], with the unchanged restricted ring. Hence $Rj_{Z*}$ is computed as $j_{Z*}J$ on a K-injective representative $J$, and its adjunction with exact restriction is [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. Exact restriction and extension by zero induce triangulated functors termwise by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated].

source.place: Section 07A5 and lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); the two acyclic-Hom calculations are written here

proof.text: Using the slice evaluation rule [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], for a module sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal E/Z$, the underived right adjoint is $(j_{Z*}F)(C)=F(C\times Z\to Z)$, with $R(C)$ acting through restriction to $R(C\times Z)$. It is a sheaf because $C\mapsto C\times Z$ takes covers and their overlaps to the corresponding covers and overlaps in the slice. Indeed a map $M|_Z\to F$ defines $M(C)\to M(C\times Z)\to F(C\times Z)$; the inverse evaluates on $C\to Z$, where $C\times Z=C$. These formulas are inverse by naturality. For $C\to U$, $C\times V=C\times W$, so $j_U^*j_{V*}F=k_{U*}(F|_W)$ as module functors, and $j_U^*j_{U*}=1$. Apply these equalities to a K-injective representative of $B$; its restriction to $W$ is K-injective by Step 4. Thus $j_U^*Rj_{V*}B=Rk_{U*}(B|_W)$ and $j_U^*Rj_{W*}D=Rk_{U*}D$, while $j_U^*Rj_{U*}A=A$. On $V$ the formulas give $j_V^*Rj_{U*}A=Rk_{V*}(A|_W)$, $j_V^*Rj_{W*}D=Rk_{V*}D$ and $j_V^*Rj_{V*}B=B$. Under these identifications the derived counits are identities on the equal complexes, and the maps to the overlap are the derived units for $k_U,k_V$. The composition identification $Rj_{U*}Rk_{U*}=Rj_{W*}$ is computed on the same K-injective complex, since $k_{U*}$ preserves K-injectives by Step 4 and $j_{U*}k_{U*}F(C)=F(C\times U\times W)=F(C\times W)$; the $V$ composition has $C\times V\times W=C\times W$.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), restriction/direct-image calculation, proved here for the slice sites using Step 4

proof.text: Put $D=B|_W$ and let $r_A:Rj_{U*}A\to Rj_{W*}(A|_W)$ and $r_B:Rj_{V*}B\to Rj_{W*}D$ be the derived unit maps for the nested restrictions, followed by the direct-image composition identifications. Define $d=(Rj_{W*}(c)\circ r_A,-r_B)$. Complete this morphism to a distinguished triangle $G\xrightarrow{f}Rj_{U*}A\oplus Rj_{V*}B\xrightarrow{d}Rj_{W*}D\to G[1]$ using the triangulated structure in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In particular $G$ is a fibre, that is a cone shifted by $[-1]$. Define $a$ as $f|_U$ followed by the first projection and the $U$-counit, and $b$ as $f|_V$ followed by the second projection and the $V$-counit.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), first triangle, with the difference sign convention specified in the item

proof.text: By Step 5 the restricted middle arrow on $U$ is $(h,-1):A\oplus D_U\to D_U$, where $D_U=Rk_{U*}D$ and $h$ is the unit $A\to Rk_{U*}(A|_W)$ followed by $Rk_{U*}c$. On $V$ identify the first summand with $D_V=Rk_{V*}D$ using $Rk_{V*}c$; its middle arrow is $(1,-r):D_V\oplus B\to D_V$, where $r$ is the unit on $B$. Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. In every degree the first map is surjective with kernel $\{(x,H^q(h)x)\}$, and the second is surjective with kernel $\{(H^q(r)y,y)\}$. Surjectivity in the preceding degree makes $H^q(f|_U)$ and $H^q(f|_V)$ injections onto these kernels. Projection therefore makes $H^q(a)$ and $H^q(b)$ isomorphisms for every $q$, so $a,b$ are isomorphisms in the derived categories (their cones are acyclic, hence zero in the localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). On $W$ the counits identify the middle arrow with $(c,-1)$. The relation $d\circ f=0$ of the distinguished triangle reads $c\circ a|_W-b|_W=0$. This is exactly the required compatibility.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), split restriction calculation; Tag 05RS (lemma-cohomology-homological); both local maps and the overlap equation written explicitly

proof.text: If $q\notin[a_0,b_0]$, exact restriction gives $H^q(G)|_U=H^q(A)=0$ and $H^q(G)|_V=H^q(B)=0$ via $a,b$. The sheaf zero test of Step 3 gives $H^q(G)=0$. This proves the common interval bound, including $a_0=b_0$ and zero inputs. It imposes no bound on the intermediate $Rj_*$ objects and makes no assertion that direct image is exact.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), local identification of the glued object; interval bound is its local-cohomology consequence

proof.text: For a module sheaf $F$ form the nested-open maps and counits $j_{W!}F|_W\xrightarrow{(i_U,-i_V)}j_{U!}F|_U\oplus j_{V!}F|_V\xrightarrow{(\epsilon_U,\epsilon_V)}F$. The composite is zero: both nested-open counits restrict to the identity of $F|_W$ under $j_{W!}\dashv j_W^*$, so they are equal. On $U$, Step 2 identifies this sequence with $L\xrightarrow{(i,-1)}F|_U\oplus L\xrightarrow{(1,i)}F|_U$, where $L=k_{U!}F|_W$. Its first map is injective, its second has section $x\mapsto(x,0)$, and a kernel element satisfies $x=-i(y)$, hence is the image of $-y$. On $V$ it is $L'\xrightarrow{(1,-i')}L'\oplus F|_V\xrightarrow{(i',1)}F|_V$: the section is $y\mapsto(0,y)$ and the kernel consists of $(x,-i'x)$. Both restricted sequences are short exact, so Step 3 gives the short exact sequence globally. Apply this natural construction to each $K^n$ of a complex $K$; naturality makes the maps commute with its differential.

source.place: Tag 08BU (lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek), omitted exactness computation replaced by the two slice calculations

proof.text: Choose a complex $K$ representing $M$. The degreewise short exact sequence of Step 9 gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. Exactness of restriction and extension by zero and [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] identify its vertices with $j_{W!}(M|_W)$, $j_{U!}(M|_U)\oplus j_{V!}(M|_V)$, and $M$. Its first two arrows are precisely the difference of the nested-open maps and the pair of counits constructed in Step 9, and its last vertex is $j_{W!}(M|_W)[1]$. Naturality of the connecting map in [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] makes this triangle natural in maps of complexes; it descends to $D(\mathcal T,R)$ because these exact termwise functors send quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, so the triangle maps associated with an inverted quasi-isomorphism are isomorphisms. This proves clause (2) for every $M$, without any morphism-gluing uniqueness claim.
